**RE: Member appeal of adverse benefit determination dated August 21, 2026**

- **Member:** Taylor Alvarez
- **Member ID:** W709290584
- **Reference number:** POC-A43FE266AD-51849
- **Service denied:** Lower back disc surgery / decompression, CPT 63030
- **Plan:** Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield (Commercial/ACA), Indiana
- **Governing policy:** *Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Spine Surgery* (Carelon) — https://files.providernews.anthem.com/4827/pdf-Spine-Surgery-2024-10-20.pdf

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for the lower back disc surgery (CPT 63030) requested by my surgeon, Dr. Reyes, MD, orthopedic surgery. The notice dated August 21, 2026 states that the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure. I am asking Anthem to reconsider that decision, because the records already in my file match the plan's own published criteria in the *Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Spine Surgery* (Carelon), which I quote below.

## The plan's criteria, and what my records show

**1. Imaging that correlates with clinical findings**

The plan's guideline states:

> "Documentation of nerve root compression or thecal sac impingement on MRI or other advanced imaging performed within the past 6 months that correlates with clinical findings"

My MRI of the lumbar spine was performed on **June 9, 2026** — within six months of the request and of the denial. It showed **L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root.**

That imaging finding lines up with what my body is doing. My records document **radicular pain into the right calf**, **positive provocative testing on the affected side**, and a **neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level**. The side, the level, and the nerve all match.

The guideline also states:

> "Imaging studies. All imaging must be performed and read by an independent radiologist. If discrepancies should arise in the interpretation of the imaging, the radiologist report will supersede. The results of all imaging studies should correlate with the clinical findings in support of the requested procedure."

I am enclosing (or can promptly provide) the complete radiology report for the June 9, 2026 MRI, read by [name of interpreting radiologist and facility — to be completed from the radiology report]. If Anthem's reviewer read the imaging differently than the radiologist did, the plan's own language says the radiologist report controls. If any part of my imaging file was missing from the packet, I ask that it be requested rather than the request denied for lack of it.

**2. Conservative management**

The plan's guideline states:

> "Conservative management1 must include a combination of strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and correct underlying dysfunction, including physical therapy AND at least ONE complementary conservative treatment strategy."

and

> "Failure of at least 6 weeks of conservative management (Physical therapy optional)"

I completed **supervised physical therapy including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility — 20 visits over 12 weeks, from April 4, 2026 to June 27, 2026**, documented in my physical therapy discharge note. Alongside that, I took **NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief**, and I had a **corticosteroid injection on April 3, 2026 that gave only about 2 weeks of partial relief.** That is physical therapy plus more than one complementary strategy, over a span well beyond six weeks.

The guideline further states:

> "Documentation of compliance with a plan of therapy that includes elements from these areas is required where conservative management is appropriate."

and

> "Patient has completed a full course of conservative management (as defined above) for the current episode of care"

I attended all 20 visits and completed the course; my compliance is documented in the discharge note.

**3. No significant improvement on reevaluation**

The plan's guideline states:

> "Worsening of or no significant improvement in signs and/or symptoms upon clinical reevaluation"

My records describe **14 months of progressive pain in the lower back, unrelieved by rest**, continuing after the full course of therapy, the NSAIDs, and the injection. The pain has not resolved — it has progressed.

**4. Radicular pain with functional impairment**

The plan's guideline states:

> "Radicular pain (radiculitis/radiculopathy) with significant functional impairment or physical exam findings that correlate with radiculopathy or nerve root compression such as:"

and defines:

> "For purposes of this guideline, significant pain and functional impairment refer to pain rated at least 3 out of 10 in intensity and associated with inability to perform at least two (2) ADLs and/or IADLs."

My records document **radicular pain into the right calf**, **positive provocative testing on the affected side**, and a **neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level** — physical exam findings that correlate with nerve root compression. They also document that I **cannot stand for more than 10 minutes.** To complete the second half of the definition on the plan's own terms, my current numeric pain rating is [pain score out of 10, from the most recent office note] and the specific activities of daily living and instrumental activities of daily living I am unable to perform are [list at least two specific ADLs/IADLs — e.g., from the most recent office note or a patient statement]. If those details are not in the packet Anthem already has, I will supply them on request rather than have the request closed without them.

**5. Other factors in the record**

My chart documents **no active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, and non-smoker.** The guideline also includes the criterion:

> "All other reasonable sources of pain have been ruled out"

I ask that Dr. Reyes's workup and the MRI findings be reviewed against this criterion, and that my surgeon be given the opportunity to address it directly if the reviewer believes it is unmet.

## A request about the criteria that were applied

The plan's guideline includes the headings:

> "Documentation supporting medical necessity and a clearly stated plan of care should be submitted at the time of the request and must include the following components:"

and

> "Initial disc herniation when ALL of the following criteria are met:"

These introduce lists of further conditions that were not reproduced in the material I have, so I cannot address every item one by one. The guideline also contains provisions on waiver of the conservative-management requirement — including "The requirement for a period of conservative management as a prerequisite to a surgical procedure is waived when there is evidence of progressive nerve or spinal cord compression resulting in a significant neurologic deficit, or when cauda equina syndrome or conus medullaris syndrome is present, and urgent intervention is indicated." — which I do not need to rely on here, because I completed conservative care in full.

I am therefore asking Anthem to **identify in writing the specific criterion or criteria from the *Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Spine Surgery* that the reviewer found unmet**, and the specific imaging finding the reviewer believed was lacking. The denial notice states a general conclusion about imaging, but my MRI is recent, it identifies nerve root compression, and it matches my exam. Without knowing which criterion was applied, I cannot fully respond, and neither can my surgeon.

## What I am asking for

I respectfully request that Anthem:

1. Overturn the denial and authorize CPT 63030 as requested by Dr. Reyes; or
2. If the denial is maintained, provide the specific guideline criterion relied upon, the reviewer's specialty and credentials, and a copy of the criteria applied; and
3. Consider this a request for a **peer-to-peer review** with Dr. Reyes before any final determination.

I understand this appeal must be received by **February 17, 2027** (180 days from the August 21, 2026 notice). I am sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, and I can also submit or check on it at anthem.com, through the Sydney Health app, or by calling the number on the back of my ID card.

**Enclosures:** copy of denial notice dated 08/21/2026; MRI lumbar spine report dated 06/09/2026; physical therapy discharge note (20 visits, 04/04/2026–06/27/2026); office notes from Dr. Reyes; injection record dated 04/03/2026; [any additional records to be listed].

Thank you for taking a second look at this. My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed, and I would like that documentation measured against the plan's own published guideline.

Sincerely,

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_
**Taylor Alvarez**
